newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka ruling coalition leads local polls.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka ruling coalition leads local polls.

text.p: Sri Lanka's ruling People's Alliance (PA) coalition looked set for victory in local polls on Saturday after taking most of the councils where results were declared, election officials said.
The PA had won 90 of 125 councils where results were declared and was leading in most others where counting was still continuing, the officials said.
Final results were expected later on Saturday, they said.

Sri Lankans voted on Friday in local polls marred by violence to elect 3,567 representatives to 238 municipal, urban and other smaller bodies in what is widely seen as the first test for President Chandrika Kumaratunga's government since it won power in 1994.
The polls have been marred by violence.
The Elections Department said 65 percent of some 10 million eligible voters had cast ballots in the election, up from 61 percent in the previous 1991 local polls.
It said voter turnout was moderate early on Friday but had picked up later in the day.

State television said a precautionary overnight curfew imposed on the capital Colombo and elsewhere was being extended until 1 p.m. (0700 GMT) to curtail post-election violence. It was originally to be lifted at 8 a.m. (0200 GMT).
Police would decide later whether to further extend the curfew, the state television said.
Newspaper reports said the PA had taken an early lead as counting began for postal votes and had later won 11 of the 15 local bodies where results were declared by early Friday.
